Blue Cheese and Walnut Tart

Served at: Old Twelfth Night Wassail

Serves 6-8Prep 15 minCook 35-40 min

A savory tart, especially one featuring robust blue cheese and earthy walnuts, makes a wonderful addition to an Old Twelfth Night Wassail. It offers a rich, comforting counterpoint to the traditional spiced cider or ale, perfect for sharing during festive midwinter gatherings.

Ingredients

  • 1 (9-inch/23 cm) unbaked pie crust (store-bought or homemade shortcrust pastry)
  • 4 ounces (115 g) blue cheese (such as Stilton, Roquefort, or Gorgonzola), crumbled
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) walnuts, roughly chopped
  • 3 large eggs
  • 1 cup (240 ml) heavy cream
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) whole milk
  • 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
  • Pinch of freshly grated nutmeg (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). If using a store-bought crust, prepare it according to package directions, typically by placing it in a 9-inch (23 cm) pie dish.
  2. Scatter the crumbled blue cheese evenly over the bottom of the pie crust.
  3. Sprinkle the chopped walnuts over the blue cheese.
  4. In a medium bowl, whisk together the eggs, heavy cream, whole milk, black pepper, and nutmeg (if using) until well combined.
  5. Carefully pour the egg mixture over the cheese and walnuts in the pie crust.
  6. Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until the tart is golden brown and the center is set (a knife inserted near the center should come out clean).
  7. Remove the tart from the oven and let it cool on a wire rack for at least 10-15 minutes before slicing and serving. It can be served warm or at room temperature.

Tips

  • For an extra layer of flavor, lightly toast the walnuts in a dry pan for a few minutes before adding them to the tart.
  • This tart pairs wonderfully with a crisp green salad dressed with a simple vinaigrette, or alongside a hearty bowl of Wassail.
  • Leftovers can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and are delicious served cold or gently reheated.
